name: VitaCore CardiaWatch Cardiac Rhythm Implant
body_location: intracardiac — embedded along the interventricular septum via catheter
description:
The CardiaWatch is a passive-to-active cardiac monitoring and intervention implant that continuously reads electrical activity across all four chambers of the heart, cross-referencing against a rolling 90-day baseline to detect arrhythmias, hypertensive episodes, and early-stage ischemic events. When it detects a deviation beyond calibrated thresholds, it delivers precisely timed micro-electrical pulses to correct rhythm, releases nanoscale vasoactive compounds stored in its onboard reservoir, and transmits an alert packet to the user's registered medical contact or nearest VitaCore-affiliated clinic. The device charges inductively from normal cardiac motion and requires no external power source under standard activity levels.

The CardiaWatch is the most commonly installed health implant in GLMZ after age forty, and is frequently recommended for younger users with family histories of cardiac disease or high-stress occupations — which, in the working tiers, covers nearly everyone. For a Tier 1 dock worker or a Tier 2 transit operator, it is the difference between dropping dead in a corridor and getting a warning buzz and a clinic referral. People with the implant describe the experience as simply never worrying about their heart again. It has become so normalized that not having one past a certain age is sometimes read as either extreme youth or extreme poverty.
installation_requirements: Outpatient cardiac catheterization clinic; requires a licensed cardiac technician; procedure takes approximately 45 minutes under local anesthetic
maintenance: Annual firmware update and reservoir refill at any VitaCore clinic; inductive self-charging under normal activity; full diagnostic every three years

side_effects: Mild chest flutter during first two weeks of calibration
Occasional awareness of heartbeat rhythm during high-stress events as the device adjusts
Rare users report a faint metallic taste when the vasoactive reservoir activates
Minor bruising at catheter insertion site, resolves within one week
cultural_context: In GLMZ, the CardiaWatch occupies the same cultural space that blood pressure medication once did — unremarkable, sensible, and slightly associated with getting older. Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents often get it through subsidized municipal health programs, and the VitaCore logo on the clinic door is as familiar as a pharmacy sign. There is a quiet class dimension: Tier 4 and 5 residents tend to opt for Helix Biosystems' more expensive cardiac suites, and some corporate wellness packages include the CardiaWatch as standard onboarding for new hires over thirty-five. Among younger users who get it early, it is sometimes worn as a subtle status marker — proof that someone takes their health seriously, or that their employer does.

story_hooks: A player's CardiaWatch alert log shows that someone in their building flatlined and was resuscitated three times in the past month — but no ambulance was ever called and no clinic record exists.

A Tier 3 insurance adjuster discovers that a batch of CardiaWatch units sold through a subsidized municipal program have had their alert packets quietly rerouted — not to clinics, but to an unknown corporate address.
A character's CardiaWatch firmware update arrives from what appears to be VitaCore but contains an undocumented behavior: it begins logging stress-response data and transmitting it to a third party.
